analyst_reports.business_description: Video-first communications platform that became the default meeting layer for businesses and consumers during a global demand shock. The entry thesis (~7 quarters ago, at the height of the surge): a category-defining communications platform riding a STRUCTURAL shift to remote and distributed work, with a land-and-expand path from meetings into a full enterprise communications suite (voice, conference rooms, contact center). Milestones: (a) hyper-growth persisting as the shock normalized (proving the shift structural, not pulled-forward), (b) enterprise/platform expansion large enough to offset any consumer fade, (c) attach of the voice and rooms products. Falsifiers recorded at entry: growth collapsing toward market rate as the shock normalizes, online/consumer churn eroding the base, and enterprise expansion failing to offset.
recent_developments: The growth falsifier has fired: quarterly YoY growth has collapsed +355% -> +191% -> +21% -> +12% (slowest ever), and the FY guide of +~11% concedes the normalization is structural, not a one-quarter air pocket.

The online/consumer segment — the surge-era windfall — is now DECLINING outright year over year, with elevated churn among shock-era monthly subscribers; management guides it to decline for the full year.

Enterprise IS delivering (revenue +31%, now ~52% majority of mix, net dollar expansion 123%, voice product past ~3M seats) — real traction, but it is offsetting the online decline to a ~12% blend, not re-accelerating the company.

Competitive pressure is heavy: the two largest enterprise-software incumbents bundle competing meeting/voice suites into their productivity platforms at near-zero marginal cost, contesting the enterprise expansion that the remaining thesis depends on.

The bull case: exceptional profitability (37% non-GAAP operating margin, ~165 FCF this quarter alone), ~1880 net cash, a buyback underway, and a ~7x forward sales multiple that is a fraction of the entry-era rating — the balance sheet and margins make this a viable standalone business even at market-rate growth.
Return-to-office has normalized meeting-seat growth; hybrid work is sticky as a BEHAVIOR, but paid-seat expansion has stalled outside enterprise accounts.
analyst_reports.macro_context: Aggressive central-bank tightening underway; the shock-beneficiary cohort is down 70-90% from highs; enterprise software budgets are under new scrutiny and sales cycles are lengthening.
